title: Creation

alternatives.label: Ussher, Masoretic genealogies
alternatives.source: Archbishop James Ussher, Annales Veteris Testamenti (1650)

alternatives.label: Old-earth readings: no datable year (cosmos c. 13.8 billion years)

summary: God creates the heavens and the earth, and forms the man and woman in his image and places them in Eden. Genesis gives no calendar date; the year shown follows the Masoretic genealogies as summed by Ussher and is a placeholder only. Many interpreters do not read Genesis 1 as giving a datable chronology at all.

title: The fall
summary: Adam and Eve eat from the forbidden tree, are judged, and are sent out of Eden; God promises that the woman's offspring will strike the serpent's head. No date is recoverable from the text.

title: Cain murders Abel
summary: Cain kills his brother Abel and is driven out as a wanderer; Seth is born in Abel's place and people begin to call on the name of the LORD.

title: Enoch walks with God
summary: Enoch "walked with God, and he was not, for God took him." Hebrews reads this as being taken without seeing death. The year follows the Masoretic genealogy and is not secure.

title: The flood

alternatives.label: Ussher, Masoretic genealogies
alternatives.source: Archbishop James Ussher, Annales Veteris Testamenti (1650)

alternatives.label: Regional-flood readings: undatable, sometimes linked to Mesopotamian floods c. 2900 BC

summary: God judges a violent world by flood, preserves Noah's family and the animals in the ark, and makes a covenant never again to destroy the earth by flood. The ark comes to rest on the mountains of Ararat. Readers differ on date and on whether the flood was global or regional.

title: Tower of Babel
summary: Humanity gathers in the plain of Shinar to build a city and tower; God confuses their language and scatters them. The setting recalls Mesopotamian ziggurats. No date is given.

title: Call of Abram

alternatives.label: Early (Masoretic, 1 Kgs 6:1 + Exod 12:40 = 430 years in Egypt)
Shorter sojourn (215 years in Egypt per LXX Exod 12:40)
Middle Bronze II setting favoured by many archaeologists

summary: God calls Abram out of Haran (having first left Ur with Terah) and promises land, offspring and blessing for all families of the earth. At Shechem God promises the land to his offspring and Abram builds an altar.

title: Abram goes down to Egypt
summary: Famine drives Abram to Egypt, where he passes Sarai off as his sister; Pharaoh is struck with plagues and sends them away. They return through the Negev to Bethel.

title: Melchizedek blesses Abram
summary: After Abram rescues Lot from four eastern kings, Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings bread and wine and blesses him; Abram gives him a tenth.

title: Covenant between the pieces
summary: Abram believes the LORD and it is counted to him as righteousness. God passes between the halves of the animals and swears to give the land, foretelling four hundred years of affliction for Abram's offspring.

title: Birth of Ishmael
summary: At Sarai's urging Abram has a son by Hagar the Egyptian. Hagar flees and meets the angel of the LORD, whom she names "the God who sees me." Abram is 86.

title: Sodom and Gomorrah destroyed
summary: Abraham intercedes for Sodom; the cities of the plain are destroyed, Lot is rescued and his wife looks back.

title: Birth of Isaac
summary: Sarah bears Isaac when Abraham is a hundred years old, as God had promised.

title: The binding of Isaac
summary: God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac on a mountain in the land of Moriah, then stops him and provides a ram. Chronicles places the later temple on Mount Moriah.

title: Jacob's dream at Bethel
summary: After taking Esau's blessing by deception, Jacob flees toward Haran; at Bethel he dreams of a stairway to heaven and God renews the Abrahamic promise to him.

title: Jacob wrestles at Peniel
summary: Returning from Paddan-aram with his family, Jacob wrestles through the night with a man at the Jabbok, is renamed Israel, and limps away blessed.

title: Joseph sold into slavery
summary: Joseph's brothers throw him into a pit at Dothan and sell him to traders bound for Egypt, where he is sold to Potiphar.

title: Joseph made ruler over Egypt
summary: After interpreting Pharaoh's dreams of plenty and famine, Joseph at thirty is set over the land of Egypt and stores grain.

title: Jacob's family settles in Goshen

alternatives.label: Early chronology (430 years before a 1446 exodus)
Late chronology (430 years before a 1260 exodus)

summary: Jacob, at 130, brings seventy persons of his household to Egypt, is reunited with Joseph, and settles in Goshen.

title: Hammurabi rules Babylon
summary: Hammurabi of Babylon (reigned c. 1792–1750 BC, middle chronology) unifies much of Mesopotamia and issues his law code, a frequent comparison point for the covenant laws of Exodus.

title: Hyksos expelled; New Kingdom begins
summary: Ahmose I drives the Hyksos out of the Delta and founds the Eighteenth Dynasty, opening Egypt's imperial New Kingdom. Some link a "new king who did not know Joseph" (Exod 1:8) to this shift.

title: Israel enslaved in Egypt
summary: A new Pharaoh fears Israel's growth, sets taskmasters over them to build store cities Pithom and Raamses, and orders the Hebrew baby boys killed.

title: Birth of Moses
summary: Jochebed hides her son in a basket among the reeds of the Nile; Pharaoh's daughter adopts him and names him Moses.

title: The burning bush
summary: Tending Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses meets God in a bush that burns without being consumed, learns the divine name "I AM WHO I AM," and is sent to Pharaoh.

title: The exodus from Egypt

alternatives.label: Early exodus (1 Kgs 6:1: 480 years before 966 BC)

summary: After ten plagues and the first Passover, Israel leaves Rameses for Succoth. The date is one of the most debated in biblical chronology: 1 Kings 6:1 points to c. 1446 BC, while the city name Rameses and the archaeology of Canaan lead many to c. 1260 BC under Ramesses II. A minority deny a historical mass exodus.

title: Crossing the sea

alternatives.label: Early exodus (1 Kgs 6:1: 480 years before 966 BC)

summary: The LORD divides the sea (Hebrew yam suph, "Sea of Reeds") and Israel crosses on dry ground; Pharaoh's chariots are drowned. Moses and Miriam sing. The location is disputed (Gulf of Suez, Bitter Lakes, Gulf of Aqaba, or a northern lagoon).

title: Covenant at Sinai

alternatives.label: Early exodus (1 Kgs 6:1: 480 years before 966 BC)

summary: In the third month Israel camps before Sinai; God speaks the Ten Commandments and the covenant is ratified with blood.

title: The golden calf

alternatives.label: Early exodus (1 Kgs 6:1: 480 years before 966 BC)

summary: While Moses is on the mountain, Aaron makes a golden calf. Moses breaks the tablets, intercedes, and the covenant is renewed with God revealing himself as merciful and gracious.

title: Tabernacle set up
summary: On the first day of the second year the tabernacle is raised and the glory of the LORD fills it; Aaron and his sons are ordained.

title: Rebellion at Kadesh
summary: Ten of twelve spies discourage the people; only Joshua and Caleb urge trust. The generation is sentenced to forty years in the wilderness.

title: Death of Moses
summary: From Mount Nebo Moses sees the promised land, dies in Moab at 120, and is buried by God; Joshua succeeds him.

title: Jordan crossed; Jericho falls
summary: The Jordan stops while the priests carry the ark across; Israel camps at Gilgal. Jericho's walls fall after seven days of marching and Rahab's household is spared. Archaeologists dispute whether Jericho was occupied in either proposed period.

title: Covenant renewal at Shechem
summary: Joshua gathers the tribes at Shechem and calls them to choose whom they will serve: "as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."

title: Othniel, first judge
summary: Israel serves the Baals and is oppressed; the LORD raises up Othniel, Caleb's nephew, and the land has rest forty years. This begins the cycle of the judges.

title: Amarna letters
summary: Clay-tablet correspondence between Pharaoh and Canaanite city-kings (including Jerusalem's Abdi-Heba) complains of the troublesome Habiru. Some link Habiru with Hebrews; most scholars see a broader social term.

title: Battle of Kadesh (Egypt vs Hittites)
summary: Ramesses II fights the Hittite king Muwatalli II at Kadesh on the Orontes, the best-documented chariot battle of antiquity; a peace treaty follows c. 1259 BC.

title: Deborah and Barak defeat Sisera
summary: Deborah the prophetess summons Barak; from Mount Tabor Israel routs Jabin's general Sisera by the Kishon, and Jael kills Sisera. The Song of Deborah is among the oldest Hebrew poems.

title: Merneptah Stele names "Israel"
summary: Pharaoh Merneptah's victory inscription lists "Israel" as a people in Canaan, the earliest extra-biblical mention of Israel.

title: Sea Peoples and the Bronze Age collapse
summary: Across the eastern Mediterranean palace civilizations collapse; Ramesses III repels the Sea Peoples, among them the Peleset, who settle the coastal plain as the Philistine pentapolis.

title: Gideon routs Midian
summary: Gideon, reluctant and testing God with a fleece, defeats the Midianites with three hundred men bearing trumpets and torches.

title: Jephthah's vow
summary: The outcast Jephthah defeats Ammon but is bound by a rash vow concerning his daughter; interpreters still debate what he did.

title: Ruth and Boaz
summary: In the days of the judges, Ruth the Moabite clings to Naomi, marries Boaz of Bethlehem, and becomes great-grandmother of David.

title: Samuel called at Shiloh
summary: Hannah dedicates her son to the LORD; the boy Samuel hears God's voice at night in the Shiloh sanctuary and becomes a recognized prophet.

title: Samson against the Philistines
summary: Samson the Nazirite fights the Philistines, is betrayed by Delilah, and dies pulling down the temple of Dagon at Gaza.

title: Ark captured at Aphek; Eli dies
summary: The Philistines defeat Israel and capture the ark; Eli's sons die and Eli falls dead at the news. The ark brings plague on the Philistine cities and is returned.

title: Saul anointed king
summary: Israel asks for a king "like all the nations." Samuel anoints Saul of Benjamin, who is publicly chosen by lot at Mizpah. The regnal figure in 1 Sam 13:1 is textually damaged, so his dates are approximate.

title: David anointed at Bethlehem
summary: After rejecting Saul, the LORD sends Samuel to Jesse's house, where the youngest son, David, is anointed and the Spirit rushes upon him.

title: David defeats Goliath
summary: In the Valley of Elah the shepherd David kills the Philistine champion Goliath of Gath with a sling stone, declaring the battle is the LORD's.

title: Saul dies on Mount Gilboa
summary: The Philistines defeat Israel at Gilboa; Saul and Jonathan die. David laments them in the Song of the Bow.

title: David king at Hebron
summary: Judah anoints David king at Hebron, where he reigns seven and a half years before all Israel makes him king.

title: David takes Jerusalem
summary: David captures the Jebusite stronghold of Zion, makes it his capital, and brings the ark up with dancing. The Tel Dan inscription (9th c. BC) later refers to the "House of David."

title: God's covenant with David
summary: Through Nathan, God promises to build David a "house" and establish his offspring's throne forever, a promise later read messianically.

title: David and Bathsheba
summary: David takes Bathsheba and arranges Uriah's death; Nathan confronts him with a parable and David repents.

title: Absalom's revolt
summary: Absalom proclaims himself king at Hebron; David flees over the Mount of Olives. Absalom is killed by Joab and David mourns him.

title: Solomon becomes king
summary: Solomon is anointed at Gihon to forestall Adonijah; at Gibeon he asks God for wisdom.

title: Solomon begins the temple
summary: In Solomon's fourth year, "the 480th year after Israel came out of Egypt," work begins on the temple on Mount Moriah. This verse is the anchor for the early exodus date.

title: Temple dedicated
summary: The ark is brought into the Most Holy Place, the cloud of glory fills the house, and Solomon prays for Israel and the foreigner.

title: Queen of Sheba visits Solomon
summary: The queen of Sheba (probably southern Arabia) tests Solomon with hard questions and praises his God.

title: The kingdom divides
summary: At Shechem Rehoboam refuses to lighten Solomon's yoke; the ten northern tribes make Jeroboam king. Judah and Benjamin remain with the house of David.

title: Jeroboam's golden calves
summary: To keep his people from going to Jerusalem, Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan and appoints his own priests and feasts, "the sin of Jeroboam" that Kings condemns in every northern reign.

title: Shishak (Shoshenq I) invades
summary: In Rehoboam's fifth year Pharaoh Shishak takes the treasures of the temple. Shoshenq I's relief at Karnak lists towns he campaigned against; a fragment of his stele was found at Megiddo.

title: Omri founds Samaria
summary: Omri moves the northern capital from Tirzah to the hill of Samaria. Assyrian records continue to call Israel "the house of Omri" long after his dynasty fell; the Mesha Stele names him too.

title: Jehoshaphat's reforms
summary: Jehoshaphat of Judah sends Levites to teach the Book of the Law in the cities and appoints judges, while allying with Ahab by marriage.

title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
summary: After a three-year drought, Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal on Carmel; fire falls on the LORD's altar and the people cry, "The LORD, he is God."

title: Elijah at Horeb
summary: Fleeing Jezebel, Elijah travels forty days to Horeb, hears the LORD not in wind, earthquake or fire but in "a low whisper," and is sent to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha.

title: Battle of Qarqar
summary: Shalmaneser III of Assyria fights a coalition of western kings at Qarqar on the Orontes. His Kurkh Monolith credits "Ahab the Israelite" with 2,000 chariots, the first extra-biblical mention of an Israelite king by name. The Bible does not mention the battle.

title: Micaiah's warning; Ahab dies at Ramoth-gilead
summary: After Ahab seizes Naboth's vineyard, the lone prophet Micaiah foretells his death; Ahab is killed by a random arrow at Ramoth-gilead.

title: Elijah taken up; Elisha succeeds
summary: Elijah is taken to heaven in a whirlwind with chariots of fire; Elisha picks up his cloak and receives a double portion of his spirit.

title: Naaman healed
summary: The Aramean commander Naaman washes seven times in the Jordan at Elisha's word and is cleansed of leprosy.

title: Jehu's coup
summary: Anointed at Elisha's command, Jehu kills Joram of Israel, Ahaziah of Judah and Jezebel, and purges Baal worship. Shalmaneser III's Black Obelisk shows "Jehu son of Omri" bowing with tribute.

title: Mesha Stele
summary: King Mesha of Moab records his revolt against Israel and names Omri and the God of Israel (YHWH); it parallels the Moabite rebellion in 2 Kings 3.

title: Athaliah usurps; Joash crowned
summary: Athaliah, Ahab's daughter, murders the royal heirs of Judah, but the infant Joash is hidden in the temple; after six years the priest Jehoiada crowns him.

title: Jonah preaches in Nineveh
summary: Jonah son of Amittai, a prophet under Jeroboam II, flees from his call, is swallowed by a great fish, and preaches to Nineveh, which repents. Readers differ on whether the book is historical narrative or a parable-like story.

title: Amos prophesies at Bethel
summary: Amos, a herdsman of Tekoa, denounces Israel's injustice "two years before the earthquake" in the prosperous days of Jeroboam II.

title: Hosea's marriage and message
summary: Hosea is told to marry Gomer, whose unfaithfulness pictures Israel's; he proclaims God's jealous, persistent love.

title: Tiglath-pileser III revives Assyria
summary: Tiglath-pileser III (called Pul) reorganizes Assyria into a standing empire and deports conquered peoples; Menahem pays him tribute and he later annexes Galilee.

title: Isaiah's temple vision
summary: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the LORD high and lifted up and hears the seraphim cry "Holy, holy, holy."

title: Syro-Ephraimite war; the Immanuel sign
summary: Aram and Israel attack Judah to force it into an anti-Assyrian alliance. Isaiah offers Ahaz the sign of Immanuel; Ahaz instead buys Assyrian help, and Damascus falls in 732 BC.

title: Micah of Moresheth
summary: Micah warns that Zion will be plowed like a field and foretells a ruler from Bethlehem; a century later Jeremiah's defenders cite him.

title: Fall of Samaria
summary: After a three-year siege Samaria falls to Assyria (Shalmaneser V, with Sargon II claiming the deportation of 27,290 people). The northern kingdom ends; Kings explains it as the fruit of covenant unfaithfulness.

title: Hezekiah's reform
summary: Hezekiah removes the high places, breaks the bronze serpent, cleanses the temple and holds a great Passover inviting northerners too.

title: Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem
summary: Sennacherib devastates Judah and takes Lachish (shown on his palace reliefs at Nineveh). His annals boast he shut Hezekiah up "like a bird in a cage" but do not claim Jerusalem's capture; the Bible records the Assyrian army struck down and Sennacherib's withdrawal.

title: Hezekiah's tunnel
summary: Hezekiah channels the Gihon spring into the city; the Siloam Inscription describes the two crews of tunnelers meeting.

title: Manasseh's long reign
summary: Manasseh rebuilds the high places and sheds much innocent blood; Chronicles adds his captivity and repentance. Kings names him the decisive cause of the exile.

title: Jeremiah called
summary: In Josiah's thirteenth year the young priest's son from Anathoth is appointed "a prophet to the nations."

title: Book of the Law found; Josiah's reform
summary: Repairs to the temple uncover the Book of the Law; the prophetess Huldah confirms its warnings, and Josiah purges idolatry as far as Bethel and keeps a great Passover.

title: Fall of Nineveh
summary: Babylonians and Medes sack Nineveh, as Nahum and Zephaniah had announced; the Assyrian remnant retreats to Haran.

title: Josiah killed at Megiddo
summary: Josiah confronts Pharaoh Necho II, marching north to aid Assyria, and is killed at Megiddo. Jeremiah laments him.

title: Battle of Carchemish
summary: Crown prince Nebuchadnezzar crushes Necho's Egyptian army at Carchemish on the Euphrates, making Babylon master of the Levant. The Babylonian Chronicle confirms the date.

title: Daniel taken to Babylon

alternatives.label: Critical: stories composed later; book finalized c. 165 BC

summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes young nobles, including Daniel and his three friends, to be trained in Babylon. Dan 1:1 dates this to Jehoiakim's third year.

title: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the statue
summary: Daniel interprets the king's dream of a statue of four metals struck by a stone that becomes a mountain filling the earth.

title: Jehoiachin and Ezekiel deported
summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem on 16 March 597 BC (Babylonian Chronicle), exiles King Jehoiachin with ten thousand leading citizens, and sets Zedekiah on the throne.

title: Ezekiel's inaugural vision
summary: By the Chebar canal the priest Ezekiel sees the glory of God on a chariot-throne and is sent as a watchman to the exiles.

title: The fiery furnace
summary: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship the golden image and are delivered from the furnace with a fourth figure among them.

title: Fall of Jerusalem; temple burned
summary: After an eighteen-month siege Babylon breaches the walls; Zedekiah is blinded, the temple is burned and many are deported. The Lachish ostraca record the last days of Judah's defense. Some date the fall to 587 BC.

title: Gedaliah murdered; flight to Egypt
summary: The Babylonian-appointed governor Gedaliah is assassinated at Mizpah; fearing reprisal, the remnant flees to Egypt, taking Jeremiah and Baruch.

title: Jehoiachin released
summary: Evil-merodach releases Jehoiachin from prison and gives him a place at the king's table. Babylonian ration tablets list "Ya'ukin, king of Judah."

title: Daniel's visions of the four beasts

alternatives.label: Critical: composed during Antiochus IV's persecution

summary: In Belshazzar's first year Daniel sees four beasts and "one like a son of man" receiving an everlasting kingdom. The date of the book is debated: traditionally Daniel wrote in the sixth century; many critical scholars date its final form to the Maccabean crisis c. 165 BC.

title: Babylon falls to Cyrus; Belshazzar's feast
summary: Persian forces take Babylon in October 539 BC. Daniel reads the writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast. The Nabonidus Chronicle and Cyrus Cylinder describe the city's fall; Belshazzar is known as Nabonidus's co-regent son.

title: Daniel in the lions' den
summary: Under "Darius the Mede," Daniel keeps praying toward Jerusalem and is delivered from the lions. The identity of Darius the Mede is itself debated (Gubaru, Cyrus under another title, or a literary figure).

title: Decree of Cyrus
summary: In his first year Cyrus permits the exiles to return and rebuild the house of God. The Cyrus Cylinder records his general policy of restoring peoples and their gods.

title: Second temple foundation laid
summary: Returnees lay the foundation; the young shout for joy while the old who remembered Solomon's temple weep. Opposition halts the work.

title: Haggai and Zechariah stir the rebuilding
summary: In Darius I's second year, the prophets rebuke the people for paneled houses while God's house lies in ruins; work resumes.

title: Second temple completed
summary: The temple is finished in Darius's sixth year (515 BC by some reckonings) and dedicated with Passover.

title: Roman Republic founded
summary: By Roman tradition the last king is expelled and the Republic founded; Rome will dominate the Mediterranean within four centuries.

title: Battle of Marathon
summary: Athens repels Darius I's invasion at Marathon; ten years later Xerxes' invasion fails at Salamis (480 BC).

title: Esther becomes queen; Purim
summary: In Xerxes' (Ahasuerus') seventh year Esther becomes queen; she later risks her life to avert Haman's plot, and the Jews keep Purim.

title: Ezra arrives in Jerusalem
summary: Ezra the scribe comes "in the seventh year of Artaxerxes" to teach the Law; he later reads it publicly while Levites explain the sense. Whether this was Artaxerxes I or II is debated.

title: Nehemiah rebuilds the walls
summary: The king's cupbearer receives permission in Artaxerxes I's twentieth year; the walls are finished in fifty-two days despite Sanballat and Tobiah.

title: Malachi, last of the prophets
summary: Malachi confronts careless priests and broken marriages and promises a messenger and the return of Elijah. Jewish tradition sees prophecy ceasing after him.

title: Alexander conquers the Levant
summary: Alexander the Great besieges Tyre and Gaza, takes Egypt and founds Alexandria. Many read Daniel's swift he-goat as Greece. Greek language and culture spread across the east.

title: Ptolemies and Seleucids divide the east
summary: After the battle of Ipsus Alexander's generals carve up his empire; Judea passes under the Ptolemies of Egypt until 198 BC, then the Seleucids of Syria. Daniel 11 traces "kings of the south and north."

title: Septuagint translated
summary: The Torah is translated into Greek in Alexandria (the Letter of Aristeas tells of seventy-two translators); the rest of the scriptures follow over the next century. The Septuagint becomes the Bible of the early church.

title: Antiochus IV desecrates the temple
summary: Antiochus IV Epiphanes bans circumcision and Sabbath and sets up an altar to Zeus in the temple, the "abomination that makes desolate" of Daniel.

title: Maccabean revolt
summary: The priest Mattathias and his sons, led by Judas Maccabeus, revolt against Seleucid rule (1 Maccabees 2–4, in the Apocrypha).

title: Temple rededicated (Hanukkah)
summary: Judas Maccabeus cleanses the temple and rededicates the altar, the origin of the Feast of Dedication that Jesus attended in Jerusalem.

title: Qumran community and the sects
summary: Pharisees, Sadducees and Essenes emerge; a community at Qumran by the Dead Sea copies scriptures and sectarian texts later found as the Dead Sea Scrolls.

title: Hasmonean independence
summary: Under Simon the Seleucids recognize Judean independence; the Hasmoneans rule as high priests and later kings, expanding into Idumea, Samaria and Galilee.

title: Pompey takes Jerusalem
summary: Called in to settle a Hasmonean civil war, Pompey captures Jerusalem and enters the Holy of Holies; Judea becomes a Roman client.

title: Herod the Great king of Judea
summary: Appointed "king of the Jews" by the Roman Senate (40 BC), Herod takes Jerusalem in 37 BC and rules as a client king.

title: Augustus becomes emperor
summary: Octavian receives the title Augustus; the Pax Romana opens roads and sea lanes later used by the apostles.

title: Herod begins rebuilding the temple
summary: Herod starts a vast reconstruction of the temple and its platform; work continues into the 60s AD.

title: Birth of Jesus

alternatives.label: Census of Quirinius AD 6 (if Luke means the known census)

summary: Jesus is born in Bethlehem in the days of Herod the Great. Because Herod died c. 4 BC (or, on a minority view, 1 BC) and Luke links the birth to a census under Quirinius, the year is debated; the traditional AD 1 rests on a sixth-century miscalculation by Dionysius Exiguus.

title: Magi visit; flight to Egypt
summary: Magi from the east worship the child; warned in a dream, Joseph takes the family to Egypt until Herod dies, then settles in Nazareth.

title: Death of Herod the Great
summary: Herod dies after a lunar eclipse and before Passover (Josephus). His kingdom is split among Archelaus, Antipas and Philip.

title: Jesus at twelve in the temple
summary: At Passover the boy Jesus stays behind, listening and asking questions among the teachers: "I must be in my Father's house."

title: Tiberius becomes emperor
summary: Tiberius succeeds Augustus. Luke dates John the Baptist's ministry to the fifteenth year of his reign.

title: Pontius Pilate prefect of Judea
summary: Pilate governs Judea (26–36). A dedicatory stone found at Caesarea Maritima in 1961 names him "prefect of Judea."

title: John the Baptist begins preaching
summary: In Tiberius's fifteenth year (AD 28/29) John calls Israel to a baptism of repentance in the Jordan.

title: Baptism and temptation of Jesus
summary: Jesus, about thirty, is baptized by John; the Spirit descends and the Father speaks. He is then tested forty days in the wilderness.

title: Water into wine at Cana
summary: At a wedding in Cana Jesus turns water into wine, "the first of his signs," and his disciples believe.

title: Sermon on the Mount
summary: On a hill near the Sea of Galilee Jesus teaches the beatitudes, the Lord's Prayer, and the call to a righteousness exceeding that of the scribes.

title: Peter's confession
summary: At Caesarea Philippi Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ; Jesus begins to teach that he must suffer, die and rise.

title: The transfiguration
summary: On a high mountain (traditionally Tabor, possibly Hermon) Jesus is transfigured and speaks with Moses and Elijah about his departure.

title: Raising of Lazarus
summary: Jesus raises Lazarus four days dead; the Sanhedrin, led by Caiaphas, resolves that one man should die for the people.

title: Triumphal entry
summary: Jesus rides a colt into Jerusalem amid shouts of "Hosanna," then clears the temple of traders.

title: Crucifixion of Jesus
summary: Betrayed in Gethsemane, tried before the high priest and Pilate, Jesus is crucified at Golgotha on a Friday at Passover and buried in Joseph of Arimathea's tomb. Astronomical calendars allow Nisan 14 on a Friday in AD 30 or AD 33; both have strong defenders.

title: Resurrection of Jesus
summary: On the third day the tomb is found empty; the risen Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene, the women, Peter, the Emmaus travelers, the Eleven and more than five hundred.

title: Ascension
summary: After forty days of appearances Jesus commissions the disciples to be witnesses to the end of the earth and is taken up from the Mount of Olives.

title: Pentecost
summary: The Spirit comes on the disciples with wind and tongues of fire; Peter preaches and about three thousand are baptized. Christians date the church's public beginning here.

title: Stephen martyred
summary: Stephen, one of the Seven, is stoned after his speech to the council; Saul approves, and persecution scatters the church.

title: Philip in Samaria; the Ethiopian official
summary: Philip proclaims Christ in Samaria and on the Gaza road baptizes a court official of the Ethiopian queen.

title: Conversion of Saul
summary: On the road to Damascus the risen Jesus appears to Saul the persecutor; he is baptized by Ananias and begins proclaiming Jesus as Son of God.

title: Cornelius receives the Spirit
summary: After a vision at Joppa, Peter preaches to the Roman centurion Cornelius; the Spirit falls on Gentiles and they are baptized.

title: Church at Antioch; "Christians"
summary: Scattered believers preach to Greeks in Antioch; Barnabas fetches Saul from Tarsus, and the disciples are first called Christians.

title: James son of Zebedee executed
summary: Herod Agrippa I beheads James and imprisons Peter, who is freed by an angel; Agrippa dies at Caesarea in AD 44 (confirmed by Josephus).

title: Paul's first missionary journey
summary: Sent out from Antioch, Barnabas and Saul cross Cyprus and plant churches in southern Galatia.

title: Letter to the Galatians
summary: Paul defends justification by faith apart from works of the law. On the South Galatian view it is his earliest letter (before the council); on the North Galatian view it dates to the mid-50s.

title: Council of Jerusalem
summary: Apostles and elders decide Gentile believers need not be circumcised, asking them to avoid a few practices offensive to Jewish believers.

title: Claudius expels Jews from Rome
summary: Claudius expels Jews from Rome; Suetonius mentions disturbances "at the instigation of Chrestus," often taken as a garbled reference to Christ. Priscilla and Aquila move to Corinth.

title: Paul's second journey; gospel to Europe
summary: Paul's Macedonian vision brings the gospel into Europe: Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea, Athens and eighteen months in Corinth.

title: Paul before Gallio
summary: Gallio, proconsul of Achaia, dismisses charges against Paul. The Delphi inscription dates Gallio's term to AD 51–52, the firmest anchor in Pauline chronology.

title: Paul's ministry in Ephesus
summary: Paul teaches for over two years in the hall of Tyrannus; the riot of the silversmiths follows. He writes 1 Corinthians here.

title: Letter to the Romans
summary: From Corinth Paul writes his fullest exposition of the gospel to the church at Rome, carried by Phoebe of Cenchreae.

title: Paul arrested in Jerusalem
summary: A temple riot leads to Paul's arrest; he is held two years at Caesarea under Felix, then appeals to Caesar before Festus.

title: Paul under house arrest in Rome
summary: After shipwreck on Malta, Paul spends two years in Rome proclaiming the kingdom "with all boldness and without hindrance."

title: James the brother of Jesus killed
summary: Josephus (Antiquities 20.200) records that the high priest Ananus had "James, the brother of Jesus who was called Christ" stoned during an interval between governors.

title: Great fire; Nero's persecution
summary: After the fire of Rome Nero blames the Christians and executes many (Tacitus, Annals 15.44).

title: Peter and Paul martyred in Rome
summary: Early tradition (1 Clement 5; later Eusebius) holds that Peter was crucified and Paul beheaded in Rome under Nero.

title: First Jewish revolt
summary: Judea rises against Rome; Vespasian and then Titus campaign through Galilee to Jerusalem. Eusebius reports Jerusalem's Christians fled to Pella.

title: Jerusalem and the temple destroyed
summary: Titus's legions burn the temple in August AD 70, ending sacrifice; the Arch of Titus in Rome shows the menorah carried in triumph. Jesus had foretold that not one stone would be left on another.

title: Fall of Masada
summary: The last rebel stronghold above the Dead Sea falls to Rome (73 or 74).

title: John's Revelation on Patmos
summary: Exiled on Patmos, John receives visions addressed to seven churches of Asia. Irenaeus places this late in Domitian's reign; some argue for a date under Nero before AD 70.

title: 1 Clement written from Rome
summary: The church at Rome writes to Corinth urging the restoration of deposed presbyters; one of the earliest Christian writings outside the New Testament.

title: Death of the apostle John
summary: Tradition (Irenaeus) says John lived in Ephesus into Trajan's reign, the last of the apostles.

title: Ignatius of Antioch martyred
summary: Bishop Ignatius is taken to Rome to die in the arena, writing seven letters on the way that stress the bishop, the Eucharist and the real humanity of Christ.

title: Bar Kokhba revolt
summary: Simon bar Kosiba, hailed by Rabbi Akiva as messiah, leads a second revolt (132–135). Hadrian crushes it, refounds Jerusalem as Aelia Capitolina and bars Jews from the city. Jewish Christians who refused to follow him suffered for it.

title: Polycarp martyred
summary: The aged bishop of Smyrna, a link to the apostle John, is burned; the Martyrdom of Polycarp is the earliest martyr account outside the New Testament.

title: Justin Martyr executed
summary: The philosopher-apologist Justin, who described Sunday worship and defended Christianity to the emperor, is beheaded in Rome.

title: Martyrs of Lyon
summary: Christians in Lyon and Vienne, including the slave girl Blandina, die in the arena; a letter describing them survives in Eusebius.

title: Irenaeus writes Against Heresies
summary: Bishop of Lyon and hearer of Polycarp, Irenaeus answers Gnosticism with apostolic succession, the rule of faith, the fourfold gospel and recapitulation in Christ.

title: Decian persecution
summary: Decius requires everyone to sacrifice to the gods and obtain a certificate; many lapse, and controversy over their readmission divides Carthage and Rome (Cyprian, Novatian).

title: Great Persecution under Diocletian
summary: Edicts order churches destroyed, scriptures burned and clergy arrested; it is the most severe empire-wide persecution.

title: Edict of Milan
summary: Constantine and Licinius grant freedom of worship to Christians and restore confiscated property, a year after Constantine's victory at the Milvian Bridge.

title: Council of Nicaea
summary: The first ecumenical council rejects Arius and confesses the Son "of one substance" (homoousios) with the Father; it also sets a common rule for dating Easter.

title: Constantinople dedicated
summary: Constantine refounds Byzantium as his new capital, the center of Christian empire in the east for over a thousand years.

title: Athanasius's Easter letter lists the NT canon
summary: Athanasius's 39th Festal Letter lists exactly the twenty-seven books of the New Testament as canonical.

title: First Council of Constantinople
summary: The second ecumenical council affirms the full deity of the Holy Spirit and expands the Nicene Creed into the form still recited, building on the Cappadocian Fathers.

title: Augustine's conversion
summary: In a Milan garden Augustine hears "take up and read," reads Romans 13 and turns to Christ; later bishop of Hippo, he shapes Western theology of grace, sin and the church.

title: Jerome completes the Vulgate
summary: Working in Bethlehem, Jerome translates the Old Testament from Hebrew and revises the Latin gospels; the Vulgate becomes the Western church's Bible.

title: Visigoths sack Rome
summary: Alaric's Visigoths sack Rome; in response Augustine writes *The City of God*.

title: Council of Ephesus
summary: The third ecumenical council rejects Nestorius and affirms Mary as Theotokos ("God-bearer"), insisting Christ is one person.

title: Council of Chalcedon
summary: The fourth ecumenical council defines Christ as one person "in two natures, without confusion, change, division or separation." Oriental Orthodox churches reject the formula, causing a lasting division.

title: End of the western Roman Empire
summary: Odoacer deposes the last western emperor, Romulus Augustulus; the eastern (Byzantine) empire continues from Constantinople.

title: Second Council of Constantinople
summary: Convened by Justinian, the fifth ecumenical council condemns the "Three Chapters" and reaffirms Chalcedon in a Cyril-friendly key; it is also associated with the condemnation of Origenist teachings.

title: Gregory the Great becomes pope
summary: Gregory organizes famine relief, sends missionaries to England (596) and writes pastoral works that shape medieval ministry.

title: Rise of Islam
summary: Muhammad's migration (hijra) from Mecca to Medina begins the Islamic calendar; within a century Arab armies conquer the Levant, Egypt, North Africa and Persia.

title: Arab conquest of Jerusalem
summary: Patriarch Sophronius surrenders Jerusalem to Caliph Umar; Christians become a protected minority under Islamic rule.

title: Dome of the Rock completed
summary: Caliph Abd al-Malik completes the Dome of the Rock on the Temple Mount.

title: Second Council of Nicaea
summary: The seventh ecumenical council ends the first phase of iconoclasm, distinguishing veneration of icons from worship due to God alone.

title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
summary: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne on Christmas Day, reviving a western empire and deepening the estrangement from Constantinople.

title: East–West Schism
summary: Papal legates excommunicate Patriarch Michael Cerularius, who excommunicates them in return. Disputes over papal authority, the filioque and unleavened bread had built for centuries; the break hardened after 1204.

title: Anselm's *Cur Deus Homo*
summary: Anselm of Canterbury argues that sin dishonors God and only a God-man can render the satisfaction owed, a landmark in atonement theology.

title: First Crusade takes Jerusalem
summary: Western crusaders capture Jerusalem with great slaughter and found the Latin kingdoms; the crusades poison relations with Muslims, Jews and Eastern Christians.

title: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
summary: Latin crusaders sack the Christian capital of the East, hardening the schism.

title: Fourth Lateran Council
summary: Innocent III's council defines transubstantiation and requires annual confession and communion.

title: Aquinas writes the *Summa Theologiae*
summary: Thomas Aquinas synthesizes Aristotelian philosophy and Christian doctrine (1265–1274), defining scholastic theology.

title: Wycliffe Bible
summary: John Wycliffe and associates translate the Vulgate into English; his followers, the Lollards, are suppressed.

title: Jan Hus burned at Constance
summary: The Czech reformer, condemned by the Council of Constance despite a safe-conduct, is burned; the Hussite movement endures.

title: Fall of Constantinople
summary: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II takes the city, ending the Byzantine Empire; Hagia Sophia becomes a mosque.

title: Gutenberg Bible printed
summary: Movable-type printing at Mainz produces the Latin Bible, making later Reformation pamphlets and vernacular Bibles possible.

title: Erasmus's Greek New Testament
summary: Erasmus publishes the first printed Greek New Testament with a fresh Latin translation; Luther and Tyndale translate from it.

title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
summary: On 31 October Martin Luther circulates theses against the sale of indulgences in Wittenberg, sparking the Reformation.

title: Luther at the Diet of Worms
summary: Before Emperor Charles V Luther refuses to recant unless convinced by scripture and plain reason; he is outlawed and hidden at the Wartburg, where he translates the New Testament.

title: First Anabaptist baptisms
summary: In Zurich, Conrad Grebel baptizes George Blaurock, rejecting infant baptism; the Swiss Brethren's Schleitheim Confession follows in 1527.

title: Tyndale's English New Testament
summary: William Tyndale's New Testament, translated from Greek, is smuggled into England; he is executed in 1536, but much of his wording passes into the King James Version.

title: Augsburg Confession
summary: Philip Melanchthon's statement of Lutheran faith is presented to Charles V.

title: Calvin's *Institutes*
summary: John Calvin publishes the first edition of the *Institutes of the Christian Religion* and soon begins his work in Geneva.

title: Council of Trent
summary: The Catholic Church (1545–1563) answers the Reformers on scripture and tradition, justification and the sacraments, and launches internal reform.

title: Heidelberg Catechism
summary: A warm Reformed catechism opening with "What is your only comfort in life and death?"

title: King James Version
summary: The Authorized Version is published in England and becomes the dominant English Bible for three centuries.

title: Synod of Dort
summary: The Dutch Reformed synod (1618–1619) rejects the Remonstrant (Arminian) articles and issues the Canons of Dort, later summarized as the "five points of Calvinism."

title: Westminster Confession
summary: The Westminster Assembly completes a confession and catechisms that become standards for Presbyterians worldwide.

title: Wesley's Aldersgate experience
summary: Hearing Luther's preface to Romans read in London, John Wesley feels his heart "strangely warmed"; Methodism's field preaching follows.

title: First Great Awakening
summary: George Whitefield's tours and Jonathan Edwards's preaching bring revival across the American colonies.

title: William Carey sails for India
summary: After *An Enquiry* (1792) and the founding of the Baptist Missionary Society, Carey goes to India, opening the modern Protestant missionary era.

title: Darby and the Brethren shape dispensationalism
summary: John Nelson Darby teaches a distinct future for Israel and a pretribulational rapture of the church in the 1830s, spreading through the Plymouth Brethren and later prophecy conferences.

title: Codex Sinaiticus discovered
summary: Constantin von Tischendorf finds leaves of a fourth-century Greek Bible at St. Catherine's Monastery, Sinai (more in 1859), transforming New Testament textual study.

title: Azusa Street Revival
summary: William J. Seymour leads an interracial revival in Los Angeles marked by speaking in tongues; it launches global Pentecostalism.

title: Scofield Reference Bible
summary: C. I. Scofield's annotated KJV popularizes dispensational premillennialism among English-speaking evangelicals.

title: Edinburgh Missionary Conference
summary: The World Missionary Conference aims at evangelizing the world and seeds the modern ecumenical movement.

title: Barmen Declaration
summary: The Confessing Church, with Karl Barth as main drafter, rejects Nazi claims over the church: Jesus Christ is the one Word of God.

title: Dead Sea Scrolls found
summary: Bedouin find scrolls in caves near Qumran, including a complete Isaiah scroll a thousand years older than previously known Hebrew manuscripts.

title: State of Israel founded
summary: Israel declares independence; the event becomes central in dispensational and Christian Zionist readings of prophecy and is contested by other interpreters.

title: Second Vatican Council
summary: The Catholic Church (1962–1965) renews liturgy in vernacular languages, encourages Bible reading and opens dialogue with other Christians.

title: Lausanne Congress on World Evangelization
summary: Billy Graham and John Stott convene evangelicals from 150 nations; the Lausanne Covenant joins evangelism and social responsibility.

title: Christianity's center shifts south
summary: By about 2000 most Christians live in Africa, Latin America and Asia, with Pentecostal and charismatic forms growing fastest.

title: Today
summary: The present: the church spans every continent, and Christians await the return of Christ while differing on the order of last things.
